issues.legal_issue: The prohibition on private coal mining operations includes the extraction of coking coal.
material_facts: Private operators claimed that the 1976 amendment prohibited mining ordinary coal but did not apply to coking coal mines.
The material they sought to extract was coking coal, which is a form of coal.
The governing legislation defined a coal mine broadly by the existence of one or more coal seams, and the related legislation defined a coking coal mine as a coal mine containing coking coal seams.
issues.conclusion: The prohibition on coal mining operations applies to coking coal mining as well as other coal mining.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(3) of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973, as amended by the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Amendment Act, 1976, uses sweeping language prohibiting coal mining operations by persons outside the specified exceptions. Section 2(b) of the 1973 Act defines a coal mine by the existence of one or more coal seams, and section 3(c) of the Coking Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1972, treats a coking coal mine as a coal mine. The Court considered the statutory text, the statutory purpose and the rule in Heydon's case; it held that legislative history could illuminate, but not confine, the interpretation.

predicates.challenge_to_coal_mining_restriction: A proceeding challenges a restriction on coal mining operations.
predicates.private_operator_seeks_mining: A private operator seeks to carry on mining operations.
predicates.material_is_coking_coal: The material the operator seeks to mine is coking coal, a form of coal.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges a coal-mining restriction and a private operator seeks to mine coking coal, the rule treats that mining as prohibited.

issues.legal_issue: Mining another mineral does not justify extracting coal where coal extraction would defeat the coal nationalisation scheme.
material_facts: It was argued that mines containing fire clay or another mineral might require mining through coal seams to reach that mineral.
The Court considered that, in such circumstances, the operation could involve extracting coal in a way that undermined the coal nationalisation measure.
issues.conclusion: Parliament may prohibit mining another mineral when the operation would involve extracting coal and could thereby defeat the coal nationalisation measure.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(3) of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973, as amended by the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Amendment Act, 1976, imposes an all-embracing restriction on coal mining. The Court held that Parliament may prohibit mining other minerals where it is necessary to prevent evasion of the coal nationalisation scheme, even if that causes an incidental injury to those seeking the other mineral.

predicates.challenge_to_mining_restriction: A proceeding challenges a restriction on mining operations.
predicates.operation_seeks_another_mineral: The mining operation seeks to reach or extract a mineral other than coal.
predicates.operation_requires_extracting_coal: The operation requires extracting coal in a way that could undermine the national coal-mining scheme.

issues.definition: When a challenged mining operation seeks another mineral but requires coal extraction that could undermine the scheme, the rule permits that coal extraction to be prohibited.

issues.legal_issue: A court may not appoint a receiver or otherwise authorize coal extraction prohibited by the coal-mining restriction.
material_facts: Receivers appointed by courts had been working mines and extracting coal or coking coal.
The statutory prohibition was imperative and comprehensive, and contravention was punishable.
The Court stated that the prohibition had been constitutionally upheld.
issues.conclusion: No court may appoint a receiver or otherwise permit the extraction of coal or coking coal contrary to the prohibition.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(3) of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973, as amended by the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Amendment Act, 1976, comprehensively prohibits the specified coal-mining operations; section 4 provides punishment for contravention. Because the prohibition had been constitutionally upheld, a court could not authorize conduct that would violate it or sanction the commission of a crime.

predicates.request_for_court_authorization: A proceeding asks a court to appoint a receiver or otherwise authorize mining.
predicates.proposed_extraction_is_coal: The proposed mining would extract coal or coking coal.
predicates.extraction_is_barred_and_punishable: The proposed extraction is barred by an enforceable and punishable mining restriction.

issues.definition: When a court is asked to authorize coal extraction that is barred and punishable, the rule requires the court not to authorize it.
